messages:
maria.design: hey team — quick design check. i sketched a compact ‘fn summary’ toggle for the run explorer so callers can collapse verbose function output but still see a one-line summary. link: https://figma.redwood/proto/fn-summary-toggle alex.devex: nice! can you paste a screenshot? small text-only toggle or an affordance with chevron? maria.design: screenshot pasted (image). thinking: show a subtle chevron + label "Summary" when compact, and "Details" when expanded. default collapsed for long tool outputs. ben.product: +1 for default collapsed on long outputs. question: how do we compute "long"? tokens? lines? sam.eng-ml: token heuristic is best for cost predictability. maybe collapse when > 200 tokens or > 6 lines. also need to preserve structured output fidelity for evals (we shouldn't hide required keys). lily.accessibility: accessibility nits — chevron-only toggles are problematic. need a visible text label, focus styles, and aria-expanded on the toggle button. also keyboard should open/close with space/enter. alex.devex: agree with lily. copy tweak thought: instead of "Summary/Details" maybe "Show summary / Show full output" — clearer when screenreader reads it out. maria.design: good point. i was trying to keep it short visually. what about label pattern: "Summary" (visual) + accessible name "Show summary of tool output"? aria-label differs from visible text. lily.accessibility: that works. example attributes we can use: ```
... full output ...
``` ben.product: sounds reasonable. one more: when collapsed, we should still surface structured keys (like status: success, trace_id) as inline chips so integrators can parse results without expanding. sam.eng-ml: yes — small inline key/value badges. e.g. `status: ok`, `duration: 12ms`, `error: none`. keep them shallow so they don't bloat the collapsed state. maria.design: UX question — where to place the badges? left of the toggle or inside the collapsed preview? current mock places them inline under the function name. open to moving them to the right of the summary line. alex.devex: put them in the collapsed preview row to keep alignment consistent with expanded output. also add tooltip on hover for truncated values. lily.accessibility: tooltips need accessible equivalents (aria-describedby) and be keyboard-triggerable. avoid relying on hover alone. ben.product: microcopy: instead of "Summary" maybe "Preview" — easier to suggest "Preview output" and then the toggle becomes "Show full output" on expand. less ambiguous? maria.design: hmm, "Preview" might be confused with run replay/preview mode. leaning to "Summary" with the aria-label approach. we could A/B test copy. sam.eng-ml: implementation note — when collapsed we can still let streaming logs append to the hidden container but only reveal the last N lines in the preview. avoids double buffering. alex.devex: great. accessibility follow-up: ensure screenreader users get a short summary of key badges when focus lands on the toggle. maybe use `aria-live="polite"` for a short announcement when state changes. lily.accessibility: careful with `aria-live` — it can be noisy if many toggles open. prefer a single polite region we update with concise text like "Output summary: status ok, 12ms" only on toggle. maria.design: noted. i'll update the figma to show: visible label "Summary ▾", aria-label "Show summary of tool output", inline badges inside preview, tooltip + aria-describedby, and a single aria-live region updated on expand/collapse. ben.product: also add a tiny ellipsis affordance that opens a menu for "copy summary", "copy full output", "open in inspector" — common asks from customers. sam.eng-ml: menu should be keyboard accessible and respect role/menu semantics. alex.devex: copy suggestions for menu items: "Copy summary", "Copy raw JSON", "Open in Inspector". keep verbs first. maria.design: thanks. i'm going to iterate the mock and push a PR for the component with accessibility docs. can folks review tomorrow? lily.accessibility: i'll do a pass on the PR for a11y. ben.product: i'll test with a few customer prompts to see if the collapsed heuristics feel right. sam.eng-ml: i'll add unit tests around the token/line break heuristic and the badge extraction. alex.devex: sounds good. small final ask — consider a compact mode in run history that hides badges to reduce visual noise for long sessions (toggle in header). maria.design: noted — will prototype a header-level compact toggle as follow-up. thanks everyone! :rocket:
